cohort: 150 newborns divided into three groups: vaginal delivery, cesarean section with general anesthesia, and cesarean section with spinal anesthesia
finding: Neonates delivered by cesarean section with general anesthesia were most prone to oxidative stress, while those delivered by cesarean section with spinal anesthesia were least affected by reactive oxygen species.
mod_finding: Neonates delivered vaginally had the highest lactate and TBARS levels (indicating higher oxidative stress) and lowest pH, PaO2, and glutathione peroxidase levels compared to cesarean deliveries.
